column_semantics.frac_eps_star: scale as a multiple of eps* (0 = unsteered baseline; +/-1, +/-2 by construction up to the 1.5*input_scale cap)
column_semantics.n: number of judged rows aggregated into this frac bucket
column_semantics.mean_g_read: mean readout g = w.h_tgt - t02 over the bucket; g<=0 means the activation is inside the target halfspace (certificate met)
column_semantics.crossed: 1 if this frac is a genuine sign change from the baseline (baseline g_read>0 AND this bucket's mean_g_read<=0), else 0 -- the baseline frac itself is always 0
column_semantics.frac_refused: fraction of completions in this bucket judged as refused
column_semantics.n_refused: raw count of refused completions in this bucket; frac_refused = n_refused / n, reported exactly so the headline rate can be read as a k-of-n and not just a point estimate
column_semantics.refused_ci95_lo: lower bound of the 95% Wilson score interval for the bucket's refusal rate (reporting only — the verdict thresholds the point estimate, see min_delta)
column_semantics.refused_ci95_hi: upper bound of the same Wilson interval
column_semantics.too_small_to_adjudicate: 1 if n < 5 (MIN_BUCKET_N), in which case this bucket cannot decide ANY verdict cell — it is still reported here with its n, never dropped; when every non-baseline bucket is flagged, no verdict is emitted at all
column_semantics.delta_vs_baseline: frac_refused minus frac_refused at the frac=0 baseline; movement is judged on magnitude (see min_delta), so a negative delta counts as moved just like a positive one. The SIGN still matters for interpretation: on refusal (label 1 = harmless) crossing is predicted to raise the rate, so see the sidecar's deciding_frac / deciding_delta_vs_baseline / refusal_fell_at_deciding_frac before reading an `actuatable`
